summary: Language agents increasingly act through external tools and interactive environments, making the interface between the model and its executable capabilities part of the decision process. summary: Foundation models are typically trained in stages: pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL), with changes in both data and learning algorithms. summary: We present EasyProver, a Lean proving system built from recursive agents with isolated contexts, asynchronous search, parallel tactic probing, and an elastic elaboration service. summary: Formula-Driven Supervised Learning (FDSL) enables vision pre-training without real images, but existing methods cast pre-training as classification on discretized labels, discarding continuity in the generative process. summary: Synthesizing a monocular video from a new camera trajectory requires preserving the observed scene geometry and motion while completing regions that become newly visible. summary: We present Youtu-Parsing-Omni, an omni-modal parser that converts documents, images, audio, and video into structured records grounded in space and time, providing a perception layer for agents that read, locate, and cite evidence across modalities. summary: Human cognition flexibly draws on a shared perceptual foundation to understand environments, attend to referenced entities, reason about spatial relationships, and act. summary: We present PhysInsert, a framework for physically plausible reference-based object insertion that jointly adapts objects and their surrounding scenes. summary: Interactive world models generate visual content conditioned on user actions, yet maintaining spatial consistency over long-horizon exploration in real time remains challenging. summary: Financial agents must form forecasts and investment judgments from decision-time evidence, with predictions evaluated against subsequent outcomes. summary: Retrieval-augmented generation commonly serves separate models for reranking and answering, duplicating model residency and passage processing. title: Kubernetes GPU Monitoring: Metrics, Challenges and Best Practices
summary: A deep dive into why GPU monitoring on Kubernetes is harder than CPU monitoring: a pod can hold nvidia.com/gpu: 1 and still sit idle, and a GPU can read 100% busy while doing little real work. The recommended path is NVIDIA DCGM Exporter as a DaemonSet, which maps metrics to pods through the kubelet pod-resources API so every metric carries namespace/pod/container labels, turning 'GPU 3 on node 7 is busy' into 'the GPU of my training job is busy'.
